$comment: Single source of truth for cross-language physics constants. Regenerate: npm run codegen:constants

kelvin.comment: metresPerSceneUnit: the dropper is drawn at 0.048 m per scene unit, so the drip tips are 0.385 m above the collectors' mouths, the columns 0.24 m apart and the induction rings 4.8 cm in radius - a classroom dropper. liquidTimeScale: 1 - the drops run on the plant's own clock. They fall the 0.385 m in 0.28 s and would be easier to watch slowed down, but the potential they fall through is the plant's, and drops shown at a quarter speed would see it swing four times faster than they should (and miss more); the sim-rate slider slows plant and drops together. nozzleDiameterM / jetSpeedMaxMS: the drip tip's bore and the jet speed at full drive; Rayleigh-Plateau break-up gives the drop (radius 0.945 d = 3.3 mm, one every 4.51 d of jet = 38 a second). surfaceTensionNm sets the Rayleigh limit on a drop's charge, 8 pi sqrt(eps0 gamma r^3) = 3.8 nC, which the induced charge reaches near 10 kV: 2.5e-5 C/kg from there on. The bore is chosen so that the streams start to miss their collectors just under the plant's 60 kV breakdown - every drop lands up to 50 kV, half at 60 kV, none by 66 kV (docs/FLUIDS.md -> Kelvin); a 2 mm bore would lose them at 30 kV and the bench would never spark. The plant's own charging rate is a classroom compression: it is some twenty times what drops at that limit could carry at this flow.

heron.comment: metresPerSceneUnit: the bench is drawn at 0.64 m per scene unit — the head each layout preset declares over the drawn span of its vessel stack is 0.62–0.67 m/unit for all five. Jet heights, particle gravity and the liquid box all use it; there is no separate 'scene gravity'. liquidTimeScale: simulated seconds per displayed second for the jet and pool — an explicit solver at this scale is only weakly compressible at sub-millisecond steps, so the liquid is shown at one sixth speed (docs/FLUIDS.md → Heron, ADR-0022).

vdg.comment: Classroom Van de Graaff lumped ODE — not an HV engineering design. C = 4πε₀r; V_break = kelvin.eBreakdownVm × gapM.

hall.comment: Classroom Hall bench: V_H = I·B/(n·e·t). Carrier profiles toggle semiconductor vs metal.

transformer.comment: Classroom coupled-inductor L-M RK4 ODE, shared by the C++ plant and the TS fallback (which is a term-for-term port of it, not a phasor approximation). Not FEM.

peltier.comment: Thermoelectric module as a cooler (TEC1-12706 class, Bi2Te3): a current drives it, heat is pumped from the cold block to the heat sink. One equivalent 1-D leg carries the whole module - seebeckVK*couples V/K, rInternalOhm, conductanceWK - resolved into legCells finite volumes (Fourier conduction + Joule heating per cell, Peltier heat at both junctions), with four lumped end nodes: cold block, cold plate, hot plate, heat sink. Z = S^2/(R*K) = 2.5e-3 /K, so dT_max = Z*Tc^2/2 is about 67 K from a 300 K hot side and I_opt = S*Tc/R about 5.2 A. sinkWK 4 W/K is a fan-cooled sink (0.25 K/W; the old generator model's 1.6 W/K cannot carry a cooler's 80 W). The cold block is insulated (coldLeakWK 0): the only heat reaching it is the load setpoint. seebeckSlopeVK2 is d(seebeck)/dT per couple about seebeckRefK; nonzero switches the Thomson term on (0 by default, so the textbook constant-property results hold exactly). iMaxA is the drive=1 current, deliberately past I_opt so the dT curve can be seen to turn over. Until the fluids epic this bench was a two-node thermoelectric generator (heater in, Seebeck power out: rLoadOhm, heaterMaxW, heatCapHotJK, heatCapColdJK) - retired with plantStateVersion 2.

mhd.comment: Hartmann MHD duct: pressure-driven liquid-metal flow braked by Lorentz drag, V = B*u*w through a resistive divider. Converged set: the C++ plant numbers (NaK-like working fluid). The duct is a thin slot - half-gap 0.5 mm between the insulating Hartmann walls, 0.1 m between the electrodes - so the 1-D Hartmann solution holds (aspect 100:1) and Ha = B*a*sqrt(sigma/(rho*nu)) spans about 3.8 to 19 over the bench's 0.2 to 1.0 T, the range where the velocity profile visibly changes from near-parabolic to a flat core. halfGapM was 0.05 until the fluids epic: that made Ha 380 to 1900, a slug at every field setting, so the profile had nothing to show. halfGapM, sigmaSm, rhoKgM3 and nuM2s feed only the reported Ha and the drawn profile; the lumped braking (lorentzK, frictionK) is still tuned, not derived. lengthM is the electrode length along the flow; it scales parcel transit time in the picture and enters no plant equation. The pre-codegen JS fallback ran a different set (pumpAccel 4.5, lorentzK 0.85, sigma 7.1e5, rho 6400, w 0.12, halfGap 0.04, nu 1.2e-6, rInternal 0.08, rLoad 0.25) - retired.

maglev.comment: Maglev gap spring-damper. JS and C++ already agreed on k/c/m; the only divergence was gravity (JS literal 9.81 vs physical.G) - both now use physical.G.

homopolar.comment: Faraday-disc homopolar generator, L-R loop with back-EMF e = 0.5*B*omega*r^2. Converged set: the C++ plant numbers. The JS fallback derived B as min(0.55, segMagnet.Br*0.28) = 0.414 T; the classroom value is now the 0.55 T the C++ plant has always used.

lorentzSled.comment: Classroom rail-motor sled (educational Lorentz-force model, not a railgun design tool). JS LORENTZ and the C++ LorentzState already agreed term for term; codegen now keeps them that way.

jumpingRing.comment: Classroom Thomson jumping ring — Lenz's law as motion. An AC primary on a laminated core drives an aluminium ring modelled as a shorted single-turn secondary carrying mass and gravity. Mutual inductance M(x) = couplingK0·sqrt(Lp·Lr)·exp(-x/couplingLambdaM) falls as the ring rises, so lift decays with height and the ring settles at a hover instead of flying away. Educational demo only: lumped circuit + rigid body, no eddy-current FEM, no temperature-dependent sigma, and no thermal state at all — the ring never heats or melts here. The drive frequency is the lab mains value in the `transformer` block, not a second literal. Shared term for term by cpp/src/plant/thomson_plant.cpp and devices/quanta/jumping-ring.ts.

pulseCoil.comment: JS-only by design (ADR-0002: no wasmMode) - TS codegen only, no C++ plant. Series R-L coil with a low-voltage capacitor-bank discharge metaphor; the armature travel is an attraction proxy, not a projectile model.
pulseCoil.chargeComment: Idle bank recharges exponentially toward drive*vChargeMax with time constant chargeTauS and auto-fires at fireFraction of that target. The charging power C*V*(Vt-V)/tau peaks at V = Vt/2, so C*vChargeMax^2/(4*chargeTauS) bounds the bank's average draw whatever the residual after a pulse; that bound is the pulse-coil energy nameplate (energyNetwork.deviceNameplateWatts).

halbachViz.comment: JS-only by design (ADR-0002: no wasmMode) - TS codegen only. Ring geometry + the segment-count / magnetisation-angle sweep the drive slider walks through. SCENE_SCALE stays in halbach-viz.ts: it is a render scale, not a physical constant.

dropTube.comment: JS-only by design (wasmMode null) - TS codegen only, no C++ plant. Classroom Lenz drop tube: an axially magnetised NdFeB cylinder, treated as a point dipole p = Br*V/mu0, falls on the axis of a thin-walled copper tube (wall w << mean radius a). Each slice of wall is a shorted ring the falling flux sweeps through; summing them gives the textbook eddy drag F = (45/1024)*mu0^2*p^2*sigma*w*v/a^4 = (45/1024)*(Br*V)^2*sigma*w*v/a^4, so the terminal velocity is algebraic, v_t = m*g/k. The same integral taken over the tube's extent (not to infinity) tapers the drag in and out at the two ends. The dipole + thin-wall idealisation is a bound to compare a real drop against, not a calibrated prediction. No FEM, no skin depth (the magnet is slow), no off-axis wobble, and no thermal state: the dissipated m*g*v heats a real tube and nothing here tracks that.
dropTube.sigmaComment: Wall conductivity in MS/m (1e6 S/m) so the setpoint slider reads in the units a data book uses: copper 59.6, aluminium 37.7, brass ~16, stainless ~1.4, plastic 0. sigmaMaxMSm is the slider ceiling.

sceneScaling.notes: Visualization layouts in src/seg-layout.js map real metres to scene units via per-preset worldScale. Plant integrators may apply additional scene gravity scaling in WASM (see sim_core.cpp).

wasmSegDefaults.comment: Default ring topology for WASM SEGSimulator only — not the visual layout presets.

energyNetwork.comment: Lab bus nameplate watts for EnergyNetwork / sim_core bus — simulated order-of-magnitude only, not metrology.

chargeCoupling.comment: Lab charge bus (ADR-0013) — lumped seed estimate, not a Laplace solve. The seed potential at the Kelvin inductor is V_sphere × r_sphere / d, the potential of an isolated charged sphere at distance d. d is a declared classroom bench separation, not the scene layout distance and not a measurement.
